newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on S. American weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on S. American weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on persistent near-ideal crop weather in South American soybean growing areas, traders said.

"Good weather in the U.S. (which hit the wheat market) and South America was the main thing," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "But it was a very dull day and tomorrow probably will be more of the same, just shorter."
The CBOT futures markets will close early Tuesday at 1201 CST and remain closed Wednesday, the Christmas Day Holiday.
The market was pressured despite a better-than-expected number for soy in USDA's weekly export inspections report.
"Exports were a little better than expected but the market is not going anywhere, it's just chopping around," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA early Monday said U.S. soybeans inspected for export the week ended Dec 19 totaled 24.8 million bushels, above expectations for 20 to 24 million.
Pressure also came from fund selling in soyoil. "Funds started selling oil and broke 23 cents in the January and that spilled into beans, but it's light volume," a trader said.
Soybeans closed two to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with January down two at $7.00 per bushel.

Traders said there were no surprises in Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report. The CFTC said as of December 17, funds were short soybeans by 89.4 million bushels and long by 95.6 million.

Refco Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of January and LFG Futures sold one million January, traders said. Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of January and bought 1.5 million bushels of March, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 32,000 contracts, below the 39,639 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 9,000 contracts, below the 10,407 traded Friday.
